
```{r setup}
library(armvar)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
```

### Samples from the Peng 2019 PDAC dataset

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data <- readRDS('~/Project/datashare/rds/00_peng_k_2019.rds')
samples <- unique(data@meta.data$orig.ident)
set.seed(1)
selected_samples <- sample(samples, length(samples)/3, replace = FALSE)
cells_from_selected_samples <- row.names(data@meta.data[data@meta.data$orig.ident %in% selected_samples,])
peng_2019_PDAC_sample <- subset(data, cells = cells_from_selected_samples)
usethis::use_data(peng_2019_PDAC_sample, overwrite = TRUE)
```

# Detection of cancer cells

### ArmVar can be executed on samples from the Peng et al. 2019 dataset that can be loaded with:

```{r} 
data("gao_2021_breast_cancer_data")
armvar_res <- armvar(data = gao_2021_breast_cancer_data, k = 300, n_pcs = 50, n.cores = 3, heatmap = TRUE, heatmap_var = c('sample', 'published_annotation'))
```

### The classification results are returned in the data@meta.data, where we can find the classification without smoothing (welch_anova), the final ArmVar classification (ArmVar_k300_pc50) and the smoothed F-statistic (smoothed_fstat_k300_pc50). 

```{r}
head(armvar_res$data@meta.data[, c('published_annotation', 'welch_anova', 'ArmVar_k300_pc50', 'smoothed_fstat_k300_pc50')])
```

```{r, fig.width=18, fig.height=5}
armvar_res$data <- Seurat::RunUMAP(armvar_res$data, dims = 1:50)

colors <- armvar::color_selection(armvar_res$data, heatmap_var = c("published_annotation"))

umap1 <- Seurat::DimPlot(armvar_res$data, reduction = "umap", group.by = 'published_annotation') +
  labs(x = "UMAP-1", y = "UMAP-2", title = "Cell type (published annotation)") +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), 
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.justification = 'center', legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors$`Published annotation`) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=3), nrow=3))

umap2 <- Seurat::DimPlot(armvar_res$data, reduction = "umap", group.by = 'ArmVar_k300_pc50') +
  labs(x = "UMAP-1", y = "UMAP-2", title = "ArmVar") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('cancer' = "#FE5F55", "normal" = "#577399")) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), 
      legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction="horizontal", legend.justification = 'center', legend.title = element_blank()) 

umap3 <- Seurat::FeaturePlot(armvar_res$data, reduction = "umap", features = "smoothed_fstat_k300_pc50") +
  labs(x = "UMAP-1", y = "UMAP-2", title = "Smoothed F-stat") +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), 
    legend.position = "right", legend.justification = 'center', legend.title = element_blank())

plot_grid(umap1, umap2, umap3, nrow=1, align = 'h')
```

### If heatmap variable(s) is/are specified, the armvar function generates an heatmap.
Note: if no heatmap variable has been specified, the heatmap can be generated with the generate_heatmap function using the data and the metadata of the armvar output.

```{r, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
ComplexHeatmap::draw(armvar_res$heatmap_obj$heatmap, annotation_legend_list=armvar_res$heatmap_obj$legend)
```

# Simulation of tumor tissue

### We also proposes a pipeline to simulate cancer cells from healthy cells by inducing CNAs.
### As a first step, foldchanges between cancer and healthy cells for genes located in chromosome arms with CNAs (according to fastCNV) are computed.

```{r}
table(gao_2021_breast_cancer_data@meta.data$published_annotation)

ggplot(gao_2021_breast_cancer_data@meta.data, aes(x='' ,y=published_annotation, fill=published_annotation)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", width=1) +
  coord_polar("y", start=0) +
  theme_void()

healthy_cells <- row.names(gao_2021_breast_cancer_data@meta.data[gao_2021_breast_cancer_data@meta.data$published_annotation=='Macrophage',])
cancer_cells <- row.names(gao_2021_breast_cancer_data@meta.data[gao_2021_breast_cancer_data@meta.data$published_annotation=='Malignant',])

filtered_data <- subset(gao_2021_breast_cancer_data, cells = c(healthy_cells, cancer_cells))
filtered_data@meta.data$ground_truth <- ifelse(row.names(filtered_data@meta.data) %in% healthy_cells, 'reference', 'cancer')

#healthy_cells <- row.names(peng_2019_PDAC_sample@meta.data[peng_2019_PDAC_sample@meta.data$published_annotation == 'Ductal cell type 1' & peng_2019_PDAC_sample@meta.data$tissue == 'h',])
#cancer_cells <- row.names(peng_2019_PDAC_sample@meta.data[peng_2019_PDAC_sample@meta.data$published_annotation == 'Ductal cell type 2',])

foldchange_computation_res <- foldchange_computation(gao_2021_breast_cancer_data, healthy_cells, cancer_cells, sample_col='sample', topNGenes=15000)
```

### The foldchange_computation function returns the metadata of fastCNV that can be visualized to ensure the proper functionning of the method. The cnv_fraction represents the amount of CNAs in the cells (more precisely the proportion of windows/chromosome arms with CNAs according to fastCNV). Here the ductal cell type 2 (malignant cells) and the ductal cell type 1 (healthy counterparts) are well separated as expected.

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
ggplot(foldchange_computation_res$fastCNV_metadata, aes(x = cnv_fraction, fill = published_annotation)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.025, position = "identity", alpha = 0.5)
```

### The function also returns a list of patterns of CNAs identified in the tumor cells. Here we can see that most of the cells are associated with unique patterns of CNAs although there are some patterns shared between 2 up to 8 cells. 

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
patterns <- foldchange_computation_res$pattern_list
shared_patterns <- setNames(lapply(names(patterns), function(sample) {
  as.data.frame(table(sapply(patterns[[sample]], length))) |>
    dplyr::rename(cell_nb = Var1, pattern_nb = Freq)
}), names(patterns)) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "sample") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = sample,
    values_from = pattern_nb,
    values_fill = 0
  )

shared_patterns$total <- rowSums(shared_patterns[,-grep('cell_nb', colnames(shared_patterns))])

ggplot(data=shared_patterns, aes(x=cell_nb, y=total)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = 'number of cells', y = 'nb of patterns', title = 'Number of patterns shared by cells')
```

### Finally we can induce CNAs in healthy cells (randomly selected) by multiplying the raw counts with the fold changes. 

```{r}
# Here we take cells from tumor tissues that are not tumor cells
#tumor_microenvrnt_cells <- row.names(peng_2019_PDAC_sample@meta.data[peng_2019_PDAC_sample@meta.data$tissue == "pt" & peng_2019_PDAC_sample@meta.data$published_annotation != 'Ductal cell type 2',])

tumor_microenvrnt_cells <- row.names(gao_2021_breast_cancer_data@meta.data[gao_2021_breast_cancer_data@meta.data$published_annotation != 'Malignant',])

simulated_seurat_obj <- cancer_tissue_simulation(data = gao_2021_breast_cancer_data, sample_nb_to_simulate=4, cancer_cell_nb_to_simulate=300, total_cell_in_sample=400, healthy_cells_to_transform=healthy_cells, tumor_microenvrnt_cells=tumor_microenvrnt_cells, sample_fc_list= foldchange_computation_res$sample_fc_list,  sample_col='sample', seed=1)

simulated_armvar_res <- armvar(data = simulated_seurat_obj, k = 300, n_pcs = 50, n.cores = 3, heatmap = TRUE, heatmap_var = c('sample', 'published_annotation'))
```

```{r, fig.width=20, fig.height=6}
simulated_seurat_obj <- Seurat::RunUMAP(simulated_armvar_res$data, dims = 1:50)

colors <- armvar::color_selection(simulated_seurat_obj, heatmap_var = c("published_annotation", "group_origin", "tumor_sample_origin"))

colors$`Group origin`[['healthy cells']] <- 'grey'
colors$`Tumor sample origin`[['healthy cells']] <- 'grey'

umap1 <- Seurat::DimPlot(simulated_seurat_obj, reduction = "umap", group.by = 'published_annotation') +
  labs(x = "UMAP-1", y = "UMAP-2", color = "Published annotation", title="Cell type") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.justification = 'center', legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors$`Published annotation`) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=5), nrow=ceiling(length(colors$`Published annotation`)/2)))

umap2 <- Seurat::DimPlot(simulated_seurat_obj, reduction = "umap", group.by = 'ArmVar_k300_pc50') +
  labs(x = "UMAP-1", y = "", title = "ArmVar") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('cancer' = "#FE5F55", "normal" = "#577399")) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), 
      legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction="horizontal", legend.justification = 'center', legend.title = element_blank()) 

umap3 <- Seurat::DimPlot(simulated_seurat_obj, reduction = "umap", group.by = 'tumor_sample_origin') +
  labs(x = "UMAP-1", y = "", color = "", title="Tumor sample origins of the CNAs \n used to simulate tumor cells") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.justification = 'center', legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors$`Tumor sample origin`) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=5), nrow=ceiling(length(unique(simulated_seurat_obj@meta.data$tumor_sample_origin))/4)))

umap4 <- Seurat::DimPlot(simulated_seurat_obj, reduction = "umap", group.by = 'group_origin') +
  labs(x = "UMAP-1", y = "", color = "", title="Healthy sample origins of the simulated tumor cells") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.justification = 'center', legend.title = element_blank())+
  scale_color_manual(values = colors$`Group origin`) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=5), nrow=ceiling(length(colors$`Group origin`)/4)))

plot_grid(umap1, umap2, umap3, umap4, nrow=1, align='h', rel_widths = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
```
